# Craft Beer School

> Craft Beer School is an India-based beer school teaching brewing, tasting, branding and the business of beer, online and in person. Based in Bengaluru, serving learners across India and worldwide.

## Courses

- [Brewing Fundamentals](https://craftbeerschool.in/brewing-fundamentals-course.html): The science of brewing: ingredients, equipment and technique. Live online sessions, plus your first real recipe. Duration 4 Weeks. Price INR 5999.
- [Advanced Brewing Science](https://craftbeerschool.in/advanced-brewing-science-course.html): Go deeper into chemistry, microbiology and advanced fermentation for serious brewers and pros. Duration 6 Weeks. Price INR 12999.
- [Brewery Business Management](https://craftbeerschool.in/brewery-business-management-course.html): The business behind the brew: plan, launch and grow a brewery, from finance to distribution. Duration 3 Weeks. Price INR 8999.
- [Style Specialisation](https://craftbeerschool.in/style-specialization-course.html): Master IPAs, stouts, lagers, sours and Belgian ales: their history, technique and award-winning examples. Duration 8 Weeks. Price INR 18999.
- [Beer Branding and Packaging](https://craftbeerschool.in/beer-branding-packaging-course.html): Build a beer brand that stands out and packaging that sells. Made for aspiring brewers and founders. Duration 3 Weeks. Price INR 4999.
- [Sensory Evaluation](https://craftbeerschool.in/sensory-evaluation-course.html): Train your palate like a pro: taste, identify off-flavours and score beer with real sensory methods. Duration 2 Weeks. Price INR 5999.
- [AI for Craft Breweries](https://craftbeerschool.in/ai-for-craft-breweries-course.html): Put GenAI to work on your brewery's copy, social posts and weekly admin, and use it responsibly. No coding needed. Duration 2 Weeks. Price INR 5000.
- [Digital Transformation Basics for Brewing](https://craftbeerschool.in/digital-transformation-basics-for-brewing-course.html): Move your brewery off paper and into simple digital tools: brew logs, stock, batch tracking and a dashboard you will actually open. Duration 2 Weeks. Price INR 5000.
- [ESG in Craft Brewing](https://craftbeerschool.in/esg-in-craft-brewing-course.html): Water, energy, spent grain, packaging, people and governance: measure what your brewery does and tell the story honestly. Duration 2 Weeks. Price INR 5000.
- [Safety in Brewing](https://craftbeerschool.in/safety-in-brewing-course.html): The hazards that hurt people in breweries and how to work around them: CO2, chemicals, heat, pressure and confined spaces. Duration 1 Week. Free (price INR 0).

## Guides

- [Rauchbier and smoked beer](https://craftbeerschool.in/smoked-beer-rauchbier.html): How malt smoked over a beechwood fire gives rauchbier its bacon like character, and where the technique came from.
- [Barleywine](https://craftbeerschool.in/barleywine-guide.html): Why barleywine is brewed strong enough to age for years, and how English and American versions split on hops.
- [What is craft beer, really?](https://craftbeerschool.in/what-is-craft-beer.html): What craft beer actually means, how it differs from mass market lager, and what to drink first. A plain English guide for Indian beer drinkers.
- [Beer styles, explained without the jargon](https://craftbeerschool.in/beer-styles-guide.html): Ales, lagers, IPAs, stouts, wheat beers and sours explained simply, with what to expect in the glass and which to try first.
- [How to taste beer like a professional](https://craftbeerschool.in/how-to-taste-beer.html): A repeatable framework for tasting beer: appearance, aroma, flavour, mouthfeel and finish, plus how to train your palate faster.
- [Beer off flavours, and what causes them](https://craftbeerschool.in/beer-off-flavours.html): The common beer faults, what each one tastes like, the process failure behind it and how brewers prevent it. A practical quality guide.
- [How craft beer actually grew in India](https://craftbeerschool.in/craft-beer-in-india.html): How India went from two national lagers to hundreds of microbreweries, why it happened city by city, and what the market looks like now.
- [How to start a microbrewery in India](https://craftbeerschool.in/start-a-microbrewery-india.html): Licences, capital, equipment, running costs and realistic timelines for opening a microbrewery or brewpub in India, without the sales pitch.
- [How to become a brewer in India](https://craftbeerschool.in/become-a-brewer-india.html): What brewers actually do, the routes into the job in India, which qualifications carry weight, and how to get hired without experience.
- [Brewing for Indian heat, water and palates](https://craftbeerschool.in/brewing-for-india.html): How heat, water chemistry, imported ingredients and the cold chain change brewing decisions in India, and which styles genuinely work here.
- [Flanders red ale](https://craftbeerschool.in/flanders-red-ale.html): How a mixed culture and years in oak give Flanders red ale its sweet and sour balance, and what makes it different from lambic.
- [Lambic and gueuze](https://craftbeerschool.in/lambic-and-gueuze.html): How spontaneous fermentation and years in an oak barrel turn plain wort into lambic, and why gueuze is a blend rather than a recipe.
- [Belgian strong dark ale](https://craftbeerschool.in/belgian-strong-dark-ale.html): What separates a Belgian strong dark ale from a dubbel, and how it stays balanced above 8 percent ABV.
- [How to read a beer label](https://craftbeerschool.in/reading-a-beer-label.html): What ABV, IBU, packaging dates and style names on a beer label actually tell you, and which numbers matter most.
- [Belgian tripel](https://craftbeerschool.in/belgian-tripel.html): How tripel stays pale, dry and drinkable despite being one of the stronger Belgian ale styles, and where its alcohol actually comes from.
- [Glycol cooling systems](https://craftbeerschool.in/glycol-cooling-systems.html): How glycol chilling actually works in a small brewery, sizing a system correctly, and the maintenance that keeps fermentation temperature stable.
- [Brewing with Indian spices](https://craftbeerschool.in/brewing-with-indian-spices.html): How to add coriander, ginger, cardamom and other Indian spices to beer without them overwhelming the base recipe.
- [How to store beer at home](https://craftbeerschool.in/how-to-store-beer-at-home.html): Simple habits that keep beer tasting the way the brewer intended: temperature, light, position and how long to actually keep it.
- [Belgian dubbel](https://craftbeerschool.in/belgian-dubbel.html): How dark candi sugar and expressive yeast give Belgian dubbel its raisin and caramel character without any roasted malt.
- [Keeping beer stable in Indian heat](https://craftbeerschool.in/beer-stability-in-indian-heat.html): Why beer ages faster in Indian conditions than brewing textbooks assume, and the practical steps that protect flavour through the supply chain.
- [Adding fruit to beer](https://craftbeerschool.in/adding-fruit-to-beer.html): When to add fruit in the brewing process, how much to use, and the sanitation and fermentation risks fruit introduces.
- [Draught line cleaning](https://craftbeerschool.in/draught-line-cleaning.html): Why a dirty beer line ruins a well brewed beer, how often lines should be cleaned, and what beer stone actually is.
- [Saison](https://craftbeerschool.in/saison-guide.html): Why saison ferments bone dry, where the peppery yeast character comes from, and how a summer farm beer became a brewery favourite.
- [Measuring dissolved oxygen](https://craftbeerschool.in/measuring-dissolved-oxygen.html): Why oxygen pickup after fermentation ruins beer quietly, how to measure it, and the packaging steps that keep dissolved oxygen down.
- [Brettanomyces explained](https://craftbeerschool.in/brettanomyces-explained.html): What Brettanomyces does to beer, the funky, farmhouse flavours it creates, and why most breweries keep it strictly separate from clean fermentation.
- [Fresh IPA versus stale IPA](https://craftbeerschool.in/fresh-vs-stale-ipa.html): Why an IPA fades faster than almost any other style, what happens to the hop aroma over time, and how to buy it fresher.
- [Amber and red ales](https://craftbeerschool.in/amber-and-red-ales.html): How caramel malt builds the colour and toffee character of amber and red ales, and where the Irish and American versions part ways.
- [A brewery QC lab on a budget](https://craftbeerschool.in/brewery-qc-lab-on-a-budget.html): The minimum quality control kit a small brewery actually needs, roughly what each tool costs, and the order to buy them in.
- [Kveik yeast for hot climates](https://craftbeerschool.in/kveik-yeast-for-hot-climates.html): Why Norwegian kveik yeast tolerates warm fermentation cleanly, and what it offers brewers without reliable cooling.
- [Running a sensory panel](https://craftbeerschool.in/running-a-sensory-panel.html): How to set up a working sensory panel in a small brewery: who sits on it, how to train them, and how to make the results actually change anything.
- [Pale ale](https://craftbeerschool.in/pale-ale-guide.html): What separates an English pale ale from an American one, how the malt and hops build the flavour, and what to look for in a glass.
- [Cleaning in place for small breweries](https://craftbeerschool.in/cip-cleaning-in-place.html): How cleaning in place actually works in a small brewery: circuits, chemistry, temperature, contact time and the checks that prove a tank is clean.
- [Harvesting and reusing yeast](https://craftbeerschool.in/yeast-harvesting-and-reuse.html): How to safely wash, store and repitch yeast from a finished batch, and how many generations you can realistically get from one strain.
- [Why breweries fail](https://craftbeerschool.in/brewery-failure-reasons.html): The recurring, avoidable reasons small Indian breweries close: undercapitalisation, quality inconsistency, distribution gaps and licensing delays.
- [Metallic off-flavours](https://craftbeerschool.in/metallic-off-flavour.html): Why some beer tastes like blood, iron or coins, and how it usually comes from equipment or glassware rather than the brew itself.
- [Session IPA](https://craftbeerschool.in/session-ipa.html): How session IPA delivers full hop flavour at 3.5 to 5% ABV, and the grain and water tricks that keep a thin beer from tasting thin.
- [Bacteria and infection in brewing](https://craftbeerschool.in/infection-bacteria-in-brewing.html): The common spoilage organisms in brewing, what they actually taste like, and the cleaning practices that keep them out.
- [Making a yeast starter](https://craftbeerschool.in/making-a-yeast-starter.html): How and when to build a yeast starter, the DME to water ratio that works, and why underpitching is behind more bad beer than bad recipes.
- [Brewing in a small Indian apartment](https://craftbeerschool.in/brewing-in-a-small-indian-apartment.html): Brewing in an Indian flat: fermentation temperature control, water sources and managing brew day smell and noise.
- [Choosing a brewery location](https://craftbeerschool.in/brewery-location-choice.html): What actually determines a good brewery site in India: zoning, utilities, excise policy and access, ranked by how hard each is to fix later.
- [When sourness is an infection](https://craftbeerschool.in/sour-infection-off-flavour.html): How to tell a deliberately sour beer from one that is sour because something got in, and why the difference matters.
- [Double IPA](https://craftbeerschool.in/double-ipa.html): What separates double IPA from a regular IPA: higher gravity, more hops at every stage, and the fermentation care needed to keep it drinkable.
- [The chemistry of stale beer](https://craftbeerschool.in/beer-staling-chemistry.html): The actual chemical reactions behind stale, cardboard and sherry flavours, and why staling keeps happening even without oxygen.
- [Dry yeast or liquid yeast?](https://craftbeerschool.in/dry-yeast-vs-liquid-yeast.html): The real trade-offs between dry and liquid yeast: strain variety, cell count, cost, and what actually changes in the finished beer.
- [Keeping a brew log that actually helps](https://craftbeerschool.in/keeping-a-brew-log.html): What to record on brew day, and why a consistent log turns single batches into patterns you can learn from.
- [Funding a brewery](https://craftbeerschool.in/brewery-funding-options.html): How Indian breweries actually get funded: founder savings, friends and family, bank loans against equipment, and what investors want to see.
- [Phenolic off-flavours](https://craftbeerschool.in/phenolic-off-flavours.html): Why clove and smoke are correct in a hefeweizen but a fault in a lager, and what usually causes a plastic or medicinal note.
- [English IPA](https://craftbeerschool.in/english-ipa.html): How English IPA differs from its American descendants: earthier hops, a firmer malt backbone, lower ABV and a drier, more balanced finish.
- [Beer shelf life](https://craftbeerschool.in/beer-shelf-life.html): What actually limits how long beer stays fresh, why temperature matters more than the calendar, and how to set a realistic best-before date.
- [Ale yeast versus lager yeast](https://craftbeerschool.in/ale-vs-lager-yeast.html): The real differences between ale and lager yeast: temperature, flavour, fermentation time, and what that means for a home brewery.
- [Brewing software and calculators worth using](https://craftbeerschool.in/brewing-software-and-calculators.html): What brewing calculators are actually good for, and where mash efficiency and water chemistry still need real data.
- [Craft beer market trends in India](https://craftbeerschool.in/craft-beer-market-india-trends.html): The directions India's craft beer market has been moving: taprooms, cans, regional growth and what a founder should actually watch for.
- [Lightstruck, or skunked, beer](https://craftbeerschool.in/lightstruck-skunky-beer.html): Why some beer smells skunky within minutes of being poured, what causes it, and why brown bottles and cans exist to stop it.
- [New England IPA](https://craftbeerschool.in/new-england-ipa.html): Why NEIPA looks cloudy on purpose, how oats and wheat build that soft mouthfeel, and what biotransformation actually does to hop flavour.
- [Oxygen pickup in packaging](https://craftbeerschool.in/oxygen-pickup-in-packaging.html): Where oxygen enters beer during filling, why total package oxygen matters, and how to keep it low in bottles, cans and kegs.
- [Brewing with RO water](https://craftbeerschool.in/ro-water-for-brewing.html): Why reverse osmosis water is a good starting point for brewing, what it strips out, and the minerals you need to add back.

- [Sustainability in brewing](https://craftbeerschool.in/sustainability-in-brewing.html): What sustainable brewing actually looks like at small scale in India: water reuse, energy, waste and packaging, without the greenwashing.
- [Oxidised beer](https://craftbeerschool.in/oxidised-beer.html): What oxidised beer tastes like, why it happens after fermentation, and why the cold chain matters more than the brewery.
- [West Coast IPA](https://craftbeerschool.in/west-coast-ipa.html): What makes West Coast IPA piney, resinous and dry rather than hazy or juicy, and how the hop and grain bill deliver that clear, bitter profile.
- [Hop creep and how to manage it](https://craftbeerschool.in/hop-creep.html): Why dry hopping can restart fermentation, how hop creep leads to gushers, and how to dry hop without the risk.

- [Acetaldehyde: the green apple fault](https://craftbeerschool.in/acetaldehyde-off-flavour.html): What acetaldehyde is, why it tastes like green apple, and why it is usually a sign of a beer that simply is not finished.
- [Milk stout and oatmeal stout](https://craftbeerschool.in/milk-and-oatmeal-stout.html): How lactose sweetens milk stout and oats thicken oatmeal stout, without either one changing the alcohol content much at all.

## Facts

- Format: live online sessions plus hands-on in-person brewery workshops.
- Online schedule: Saturdays and Sundays, 12:00 PM to 2:00 PM IST, max 20 students per batch.
- Certificate of Completion needs all assignments and at least 80% attendance.
- Certification support: WSET and Cicerone preparation.
- Cohorts are deliberately small, with one-to-one mentorship.
- Contact: chatty@cheerschattyventures.com, +91-98209-25347.
